info.title: Wirepas locations metadata service API
info.description: API for the Wirepas location metadata management service

get.description:
Returns list of location resources. It is recommended that the client implements the get requests based
on the client defined "typing" (using the locationTypeUuid field). Furthermore, client shall sort and page
the results accordingly to avoid excess load on the service and communications media.

This endpoint supports simple queries with reasonable set of different filter parameters. In case of more
complex queries, separate search endpoint shall be used.

See advanced search for supported query fields and pattern matching.

parameters.name: sortBy
parameters.description:
The field according to which the response data shall be sorted. By default, results are sorted by the "name" field.

**NOTE:** Sequence numbering should be used for sorting only in scenarios, where other search parameters
limit the result set so that sequence numbers can be expected to be unique.

results.description:
Actual results, i.e. the list of locations matching the request parameters. Note that the list might not be full
result set but contain only a partial result set (more information in metadata)

post.summary: Create a new location or locations
post.description: Create a new location object or a list of locations with provided parameters.

201.description: New location object(s) have been created.

patch.summary: Update one or multiple location objects
patch.description:
Update the attributes of one or multiple location objects. The items in the list are all updated and the return value
of the operation reflects the success of the whole operation. Thus, all items in the list are either updated as requested
by the operation, or no changes are made in any of the items in case of an error. All the location objects identified in
the operation shall be found, otherwise the operation will fail.

The items may not be complete location objects, thus only those fields that are given are updated. It is not possible to remove
an attribute from a location with this operation. If that kind of functionality is needed, an update operation (PUT) of a specific
location object shall be used.

delete.summary: Deletes one or multiple location object(s)
delete.description:
Deletes one or multiple location objects based on the query filter attributes given as a parameters for the request. All
location objects matching the given query are removed, thus caution should be exercised when using this operation. The
return value reflects the success of the whole operation, thus either all location objects matching the query are removed
or none is removed in case of an error.

The success of the operation is based on the requested target state, e.g. if the deletion is requested based on UUID
of a location object, the operation for that location object is successful also in a case where the given location does
not exist (anymore).

See advanced search for supported query fields and pattern matching.

200.description: Location objects matching the query are deleted.

post.description:
Search for location objects with complex query parameters and conditions. The filtering and search conditions are defined
in the request body using RSQL / FIQL, see short description from here:
[https://github.com/jirutka/rsql-parser#grammar-and-semantic](https://github.com/jirutka/rsql-parser#grammar-and-semantic)

It is worth pointing out that this operation does not change the server state nor it does not save the query.
Instead, the operation is purposed solely for providing more freedom in the definition of complex search filter
conditions in cases where the basic filtering with query parameters would end up to extremely long URLs.

Queries are case-insensitive. Pattern matching is supported in the query: an asterisk sign ('*') can be used to match zero
or more arbitrary characters. Plain asterisk query (e.g. `name==*`) can be used for excluding null items.

If your operator is one of following <, >, <= or >= and your comparison string is only digits you can use "str(string)" to ensure it
is treated as a string e.g. name>="str(123)". Nested fields can be accessed with a dot operator e.g. `approxCoordinates.latitude`.

The query rules shall use the property field names of the Location resource/object.

sortBy.description: The field according to which the response data shall be sorted. By default, results are sorted by the "name" field.

query.description:
More detailed search query for limiting the request to subset of locations based on the defined filters.
The syntax of the query is based on RSQL / FIQL, which is shortly described in here:
[https://github.com/jirutka/rsql-parser#grammar-and-semantic](https://github.com/jirutka/rsql-parser#grammar-and-semantic)

See more details in operation description.

200.description: A list of location objects matching the query given in the request body.

results.description:
Actual results, i.e. the list of location objects matching the query given in the request body. Note that the list
might not be full result set but contain only a partial result set (more information in metadata)

get.summary: Obtain information about a location object
get.description: Obtain information about a specific location object identified by the UUID

parameters.name: locationUuid
parameters.description: UUID identifying the location object the operation is targeted to

200.description: Successfully returned information of the requested location object.

put.description: Update a specific location identified by UUID with a provided object (complete object)

parameters.name: locationUuid
parameters.description: UUID identifying the location object the operation is targeted to

patch.description:
Update the given fields in a specific location object identified by UUID.

**NOTE:** The item given in the body may not be a complete location object, thus only those fields that are given are updated.

parameters.name: locationUuid
parameters.description: UUID identifying the location object the operation is targeted to

parameters.name: locationUuid
parameters.description: UUID identifying the location object the operation is targeted to

204.description: Location object deleted successfully or already deleted.

get.summary: Get a list of location types
get.description:
Returns list of location types. It is expected that the number of location types is rather limited, thus paging and
sorting of the results is not supported. Filtering of the results is according to different attributes is supported.
The filtering conditions are defined in the query parameter using RSQL / FIQL, see more details from query filter
description.

Queries are case-insensitive. Pattern matching is supported in the query: an asterisk sign ('*') can be used to match zero
or more arbitrary characters. Plain asterisk query (e.g. `name==*`) can be used for excluding null items.

If your operator is one of following <, >, <= or >= and your comparison string is only digits you can use "str(string)" to ensure
it is treated as a string e.g. name>="str(123)".

The query rules shall use the property field names of the location type resource.

200.description: A list of location type objects.

post.summary: Create a new location type or types
post.description: Create a new location type object or a list of location types with provided parameters.

201.description: New location type object(s) have been created.

delete.summary: Deletes one or multiple location type object(s)
delete.description:
Deletes one or multiple location type objects based on the query filter attributes given as a parameters for the request.
All location type objects matching the given query are removed, thus caution should be exercised when using this operation.
The return value reflects the success of the whole operation, thus either all location type objects matching the query are
removed or none is removed in case of an error.

The success of the operation is based on the requested target state, e.g. if the deletion is requested based on UUID of a
location type object, the operation for that type is successful also in a case where the given location type does not exist
(anymore).

**NOTE:** A location type cannot be deleted, if it is assigned to some location object. Thus, in order to remove a location
type, locations with that type needs to be first updated with a new type.

200.description: Location type objects matching the query are deleted.

get.summary: Obtain information about a location type object
get.description: Obtain information about a specific location type object identified by the UUID

parameters.name: locationTypeUuid
parameters.description: UUID identifying the location type object the operation is targeted to

200.description: Successfully returned information of the requested location type object.

put.description:
Update a specific location type identified by UUID with a provided object (complete object)

**NOTE:** Changing the parent hierarchy is not allowed, if the location type is assigned to any location. This restriction
is to prevent incorrect parent references between the actual location objects.

parameters.name: locationTypeUuid
parameters.description: UUID identifying the location type object the operation is targeted to

patch.summary: Partially/patch update the location type object
patch.description:
Update the given fields in a specific location type object identified by UUID. It is worth noting, that the item given in
the body may not be a complete location object, thus only those fields that are given are updated.

**NOTE:** Changing the parent hierarchy is not allowed, if the location type is assigned to any location. This restriction
is to prevent incorrect parent references between the actual location objects.

parameters.name: locationTypeUuid
parameters.description: UUID identifying the location type object the operation is targeted to

delete.description:
Delete the location type object identified by the UUID.

**NOTE:** A location type cannot be deleted, if it is assigned to some location object. Thus, in order to remove a location
type, locations with that type needs to be first updated with a new type.

parameters.name: locationTypeUuid
parameters.description: UUID identifying the location type object the operation is targeted to

204.description: Location type object deleted successfully or already deleted.

PagingQueryLimit.name: limit
PagingQueryLimit.description:
Number of items to return in a single response. If the total number of results matching the query / request
then the results are limited to the given amount. In that case, the service will provide cursors that allow
traversing between the pages.

**NOTE:** It is highly recommended to use reasonable page sizes especially if connecting from a client
application. However, the maximum value for the limit is kept quite high in order to ease integration of
customer backend services.

PagingQueryCursor.name: cursor
PagingQueryCursor.description: Cursor pointing to the next / first item to be returned

QueryFilter.name: query
QueryFilter.description:
More detailed search query for limiting the request to subset of nodes based on the defined filters.
The syntax of the query is based on RSQL / FIQL, which is shortly described in here:
[https://github.com/jirutka/rsql-parser#grammar-and-semantic](https://github.com/jirutka/rsql-parser#grammar-and-semantic)

Note that the maximum length of the query string in the parameters is limited. If more advanced search parameters are
required, use the dedicated search endpoint if available.

Queries are case-insensitive. Pattern matching is supported in the query filter: an asterisk sign ('*') can be used to match
zero or more arbitrary characters. Plain asterisk query (e.g. `name==*`) can be used for excluding null items.

If your operator is one of following <, >, <= or >= and your comparison string is only digits you can use "str(string)" to ensure it is treated as a string e.g. name>="str(123)".
Nested fields can be accessed with a dot operator: `parent.children`

DeleteQueryFilter.name: query
DeleteQueryFilter.description:
Detailed query for limiting the delete request to a subset of nodes based on the defined filters. The syntax of the query is
based on RSQL / FIQL similarly to search queries. RSQL is shortly described in here:
[https://github.com/jirutka/rsql-parser#grammar-and-semantic](https://github.com/jirutka/rsql-parser#grammar-and-semantic)

Explicit query filter is required parameter for the delete queries. Thus, performing a delete operation for multiple resources
at a time is not allowed without the query limiting the targeted entities. Wildcards etc. are allowed to target a larger set
of nodes.

See search query for more detailed description of the syntax and supported fields.

SortingQueryOrder.name: order
SortingQueryOrder.description:
Desired ordering of sorted results, either `asc` (ascending) or `desc` (descending). By default, results are sorted in
ascending order (`asc`).

QuerySelection.name: fields
QuerySelection.description: Desired selection of fields to be returned with results. Uuid and sortBy field are always selected by default.

QueryTotalResults.name: totalResultsCountOnly
QueryTotalResults.description:
When this parameter is given and set to `true`, the query response contains only the metadata part with the `totalResultsCount` field giving the count of objects matching
the query filter in the request. When this parameter is given, `cursor` and `fields` parameters are not allowed. Other parameters (like `limit`) are ignored.

uuid.description: Globally unique ID (UUID) used for identifying the API resource

modificationTime.description: Epoch timestamp for the last modification time of the object

name.description:
Short descriptive name for the metadata resource. If not explicitly set, the system will generate the
name based on the low level identifier of the resource.

description.description:
More versatile description of the metadata resource. This is optional information, i.e. there is no
default content for this field.

custom.description:
A freeform dictionary that clients can utilize for storing their own metadata related to the managed resource.
The main intention of the custom fields is to allow clients to manage the relations between the client side data
objects and corresponding Wirepas NMS data object. Thus, client can e.g. add a custom field for storing the
internal identifier of managed asset to which the corresponding Wirepas node or gateway is linked to. Naturally,
as the fields are fully customizable other usage purposes are possible.

The data management of the custom fields differ slightly from other fields or attributes in managed resources or
objects. The main difference is that the contents of `custom` field itself shall always be considered as single
managed field. Thus, when adding new fields as well as when updating or removing existing fields to/from the `custom`,
all the custom fields shall be given. I.e. the provided custom fields directly reflect the end state of the whole
`custom` field after the operation. This is mainly relevant for PATCH update operations, which differ from other fields.

locationTypeUuid.description:
Type of the location object. This is a UUID reference to location type object representing the type of this
location object.

sequenceNumber.description:
Optional indexing number for the location objects, which may be used by client to define the ordering of the
the given type of location objects under their parent relation.

Simple examples for the ordering are e.g. numbered buildings within a specific site, like Building 1, Building 2
(or Building A, Building B), etc. or for example floors within a building (Ground floor, 1st floor, 2nd floor, ...)

Following should be noted related to the sequence numbering:
* Sequence numbers under a parent reference should be unique, but it is on the responsibility of the client
  to guarantee this.
* Sequence numbers do not need to be consecutive but the usage is totally up to the client

allOf.description:
Approximated center coordinates of this location. This can be used to roughly tie the location to a real world
position in those cases where it is applicable (e.g. like with sites and buildings). Note that these coordinates
are not used for any positioning related calculations, but instead they facilitate the mapping of this location
object, help in searching of different locations in an area, etc.

parentLocationUuid.description:
An UUID reference to the parent location resource, to which this location is related to. The given parent shall follow
the hierarchy defined by the location type hierarchy.

LocationTypeModel.description:
Location type enables the creation of typed hierarchy for the location objects. The types and therefore the
levels of hierarchy and their relations are not limited. Each type can have only one parent, thus making it
possible to create tree like structures with one or more root types.

The purpose of the location types is to provide means to model real world concepts to the system. These can
be for example geospatial areas within a country, like states, districts and cities, or somewhat narrower
context within a manufacturing facilities, like sites, buildings, warehouses, etc.

Following gives a couple of concrete examples of different typings.

Simple hierarchy with sequential order:

```
COUNTRY -> STATE -> DISTRICT -> CITY
```

An example of a tree type of hierarchy:

```
SITE -> BUILDING -> FLOOR
     `> PARKING
```

After location types are defined, these can be then assigned to locations. When setting parent linkage to a
single location, it is checked that it follows also the type hierarchy.

parentTypeUuid.description:
An UUID reference to the parent location location type for building the location type hierarchy. A location type
can have only one parent type, creating a tree like structure for location types. For root location type(s), this
field is empty.

isFilterType.description:
Flag indicating, that the locations of this type should be included in the location filtering.

The flag defaults to true.

isSequential.description:
Flag indicating, whether the locations of this type are such that they are ordered under their parent relation.

The flag defaults to false.

Simple examples for the ordering are e.g. numbered buildings within a specific site, like Building 1, Building 2
(or Building A, Building B), or for example floors within a building (Ground floor, 1st floor, 2nd floor, ...)

LocationGeometryType.description:
Defines the type of the geospatial location (coordinates) definition for the location objects of this type. If set, all
location objects created with this type shall allow only defining geometry of that type. Defaults to AREA_POLYGON.

Possible geometry types are:

- `CENTER_POINT`: Approximated central coordinate point of the location
- `AREA_POLYGON`: Area boundaries defined as a polygon
- `NONE`: Reserved for location types that do not have geospatial reference (like organizations etc.)

Coordinates.description:
A presentation of a coordinate point used to either denote a single location or alternatively
a point in a area, like bounding box.

**NOTE:** In the current version, the coordinates are given in WGS84 coordinate system (EPSG:4326),
but for future compatibility, an option to support multiple coordinate systems is preserved.

latitude.description: Decimal presentation of the latitude (in given coordinate system)

longitude.description: Decimal presentation of the longitude (in given coordinate system)

altitude.description: Altitude in meters above sea level

EpsgCode.description:
EPSG code of the coordinate system used to represent latitude and longitude. The available options are
limited to those supported by the services. Currently available EPSG codes are following:
* `EPSG:4326`: WGS84 (default)

limit.description:
Number of items to return in a single response. If the total number of results matching the query / request
then the results are limited to the given amount. In that case, the service will provide cursors that allow
traversing between the pages.

**NOTE:** It is highly recommended to use reasonable page sizes especially if connecting from a client
application. However, the maximum value for the limit is kept quite high in order to ease integration of
customer backend services.

cursor.description: Cursor pointing to the next / first item to be returned

order.description: Desired ordering of sorted results, either `asc` (ascending) or `desc` (descending)

fields.description: Desired selection of fields to be returned with results. Uuid and sortBy field are always selected by default.

totalResultsCountOnly.description: If set to true, only total results count matching query, ignoring cursor is returned in metadata response.

ErrorResponse.description: Common error response resource sent in case of server error

message.description: Short descriptive error message in English

allOf.description:
More detailed information about the error if seen necessary. The information provided in the details
depends on the Wirepas error given in the errorCode (see more information from the error code
descriptions). If no details are available, then the details field is not given or is empty. The
details field is encoded in JSON format. If the input was list type, then also the details field is
a list containing one or more items with error. With operations accessing a single resource, the
details field contains only a single object (not an array). The possible fields in each of the item
in the details are described per error code in the Wirepas error code descriptions.

serviceRef.description:
Error reference identifier, which makes it possible locate related error message from server side logs.
This is mainly purposed for development time use, but can be benefit also when tracking production system
problems.

serviceId.description: Identifier of the backend service instance being a source of the error

errorRef.description: UUID type of reference to the error, which can be used to track error from server side

WirepasErrorCode.description:
More detailed error codes describing the reason for failures. These error codes are specific
to Wirepas backend services. The main objective of the error codes is to give more information
related to the potential cause of an failure in operation. These can be then benefit e.g. when
giving error indications to actual end users, in internalization of error responses etc.

The error codes are mainly related to the scenarios, where server returns HTTP error 400 (Bad
Request) or 500 (Internal Server Error). However, an Wirepas error code might be included also in
other errors, but the added information in these cases might be quite minimal.

The Wirepas error codes can be categorized to following groups:
* **Client data errors**: Error codes describing the erroneous data provided by the client
* **Client request errors**: Other client request related error codes
* **System error codes**: Error codes giving some background on potential system level problems

In some of the cases, the details field may contain more information about the error. The details
field is encoded in JSON format. The contents do not have standard format, thus parsing it is not
recommended. Instead, it is purposed mainly for development time and debug purposes for providing
more insights to the actual cause of the error.

The actual error codes are listed below per category.

**Client data errors**:
* `WERR_UNKNOWN_RESOURCE`: Identified request object(s) are not found from the system. Details field
  in the response may identify the unknown resources.
* `WERR_UNKNOWN_FIELD`: Request object(s) contain unknown fields. Details field in the response may
  identify the unknown resources.
* `WERR_INVALID_FIELD_VALUE`: Values of field(s) in the request is not acceptable. Details may contain
  information identifying the resources and fields involved.
* `WERR_INVALID_IDENTIFIER`: The value given for the identifier field in an object is invalid. This does not
  refer to the UUID of the object but the real world identifiers (such as network or node addresses). Details
  field may contain additional information about the error.
* `WERR_DUPLICATE_IDENTIFIER`: The identifier for an object is already allocated and therefore does not meet
  the unique constraint. This does not refer to the UUID of the object but the real world identifiers (such
  as network and node addresses). Details field may contain additional information about the error.
* `WERR_INVALID_REFERENCE`: The reference object identifier given in the request is invalid or cannot be
  found. Details may contain more information about erroneous objects and references.
* `WERR_RESOURCE_IN_USE`: The resource being deleted is in use or referenced by another object so that it
  cannot be deleted before it is freed or references removed.

**Client request errors**:
* `WERR_API_VALIDATION`: The request does not meet the requirements and constraints defined by the API
  specification. Typical causes are e.g. malformed content, missing required fields, incorrect types or enum
  fields, or illegal values not meeting the given (e.g. min/max) constraints.
* `WERR_INVALID_CREDENTIALS`: The credentials provided with the client request are not available or invalid.
* `WERR_ACCESS_NOT_ALLOWED_OPERATION`: The client does not have enough rights to perform the requested operation.
* `WERR_ACCESS_NOT_ALLOWED_DATA`: The client does not have rights to access the requested resource.
* `WERR_INVALID_PARAMETERS`: The URL parameters given for the request are invalid. The details may contain
  a list of invalid parameters (InvalidParams).
* `WERR_INVALID_HEADERS`: The header fields in request are invalid, contain invalid values, etc. The details
  may contain a list of invalid parameters (InvalidParams).
* `WERR_INVALID_CONTENT`: The content body of the request has invalid format / encoding.
* `WERR_CONTENT_TOO_LARGE`: The provided content body is too large for the service to handle.
* `WERR_MISSING_CONTENT`: The content is missing for a request that expects to have content.
* `WERR_INVALID_QUERY`: The query filter given as a parameter for GET or advanced search request has invalid
  syntax or contain invalid fields. Details may contain a list of invalid fields (errorFields).
* `WERR_INVALID_QUERY_PARAMETERS`: Some of the other parameters for the search query (limit, sortBy, order,
  or cursor) is incorrect or mismatches against other fields (e.g. cursor not matching the current parameters).
* `WERR_INVALID_STATE`: The requested state change operation of an object is not allowed given the current
  state of the target resource.
* `WERR_STATE_CHANGE_NOT_ALLOWED`: The requested state change operation was not allowed (see message for further details).
* `WERR_FAILED_RESOURCES`: The requested operation failed because there are or were failed resources or operations that
  need to be managed before continuing.
* `WERR_OVERLAPPING_OPERATION`: The requested operation failed, since there is an overlapping operation preventing the
  requested operation.
* `WERR_PRECONDITION_ERROR`: The requested operation failed because needed preconditions were not met.
  The error cannot be bypassed with the force flag, instead the fulfilling of the preconditions must be waited on.
* `WERR_PRECONDITION_VALIDATION`: The requested operation failed because needed preconditions were not met,
  but the error can be bypassed using the force flag.

**System error codes**:
* `WERR_DATABASE_ERROR`: The requested operation failed due to a database connection or request failure. See
  more details on the backend system logs.
* `WERR_MESSAGING_ERROR`: The requested operation failed due to an internal messaging error at the backend. See
  more details on the backend system logs.
* `WERR_OPERATION_TIMEOUT`: The requested operation failed due to an internal operation timeout. See more
  details on the backend system logs.
* `WERR_GENERAL_ERROR`: The requested operation failed due to an unknown internal error at the backend. See
  more details on the backend system logs.

totalResultsCount.description:
Total number of items matching the given query. This field is only available in the response
when totalResultsCountOnly=true is given as a query parameter. Cursor values are not returned
in the response.

DeleteListResponse.description: List of deleted items and metadata related to the delete operation

deletedItems.description: The list of UUIDs identifying the items that were deleted.

deletedCount.description: Number of items deleted with this operation

resultsCount.description: The number of items returned in the result list.

nextCursor.description:
A cursor pointing to the "next" data set, i.e. this should be given as a cursor parameter
in the following request to get the following page in results. This is empty, if there is no
following page.

prevCursor.description:
A cursor pointing to the "previous" data set, thus when traversing backwards within the result
set, this should be given as a cursor parameter in the following request. When this is empty,
there is no previous page.

BadRequest.description:
Error caused by invalid client request. Potential causes are malformed request, invalid data
fields, potential conflicts in data, etc.

More details for the potential reason of the error are given by the Wirepas error in `errorCode`
field in error response.

Unauthorized.description:
Client did not provide required credentials with the request and is thus not unauthorized perform
the request. Client may attempt the operation again after authenticating.

value.message: None or invalid credentials provided in the request.

Forbidden.description:
Client is not authorized to complete the request. The permissions granted to the client during the
authentication do not allow either performing the requested operation (e.g. POST) or access the
requested resource object.

More details for the potential reason of the error are given by the Wirepas error in `errorCode`
field in error response.

value.message: Not enough privileges to perform requested operation

NotFound.description:
Requested resource is not found from the server. This can be caused either by invalid URL or by the fact
that the resource identified by the UUID is not anymore found from the server.

This response may not contain additional error response content.

Conflict.description:
Error caused by client request that is conflicting with the current server state. This error can be caused e.g.
by an attempt to modify a non-changeable identifier field, a delete request to an object that is referenced by
another object with as a mandatory requirement, or an invalid state transition request.

More details for the potential reason of the error are given by the Wirepas error in `errorCode`
field in error response.

value.message: Identifier cannot be changed once set.

InternalServerError.description:
Internal server error occurred during the processing of the request. In general, this is caused by some
unexpected system error (e.g. unavailability of system resources, database problems, etc.).

More details for the potential reason of the error are given by the Wirepas error in `errorCode`
field in error response.

DefaultErrorResponse.description:
Unexpected error when handling the request. More details about the potential reason of the error are
given by the HTTP error code. See e.g. https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Status for list
of all HTTP error codes.

The response may not contain additional error response content in the message body.
